unclear: Top-level model: ControlLDM (a LatentDiffusion subclass) is the system; its apply_model runs ControlNet then ControlledUnetModel. UNetModel.forward in openaimodel.py is the plain SD forward that ControlledUnetModel overrides.

REPO holds only cldm/cldm.py and ldm/modules/diffusionmodules/openaimodel.py. LatentDiffusion (training step: q_sample noising and the loss), DDIMSampler, util.py (zero_module, conv_nd, timestep_embedding), attention.py (SpatialTransformer), the text-encoder and autoencoder classes, configs and training/inference scripts are absent. So noise ϵ, z_0 and the loss are not recorded here, the text encoder's CLIP identity rests on the draft, and zero_module 'zeroing the weights' rests on its name (its body is not in REPO).

Config values are not in REPO: model_channels, in_channels, out_channels, hint_channels, num_res_blocks (no default), attention_resolutions (no default), context_dim, num_heads/num_head_channels, the actual channel_mult (default (1, 2, 4, 8)), use_spatial_transformer (default False), only_mid_control, sd_locked. Channel labels are therefore written as model_channels·mult[k].

The grouping into 4 levels of 3 blocks (l1..l4) assumes len(channel_mult) = 4 and num_res_blocks = 2: with the default 4 levels this is the only choice that gives 12 input blocks + 1 middle = 13 outputs, matching control_scales = [1.0] * 13. zip() at apply_model silently truncates, so a mismatch would not raise.

Where the hint enters differs from the draft: guided_hint is added to the OUTPUT of the trainable copy's first input block (input_blocks[0], a 3×3 conv of x_noisy), not to x before the trainable copy; that sum feeds input_blocks[1] and zero_convs[0].

Hint encoder differs from the draft (paper text): 8 convs, not 4. There are 7 3×3 convs (16, 16, 32, 32, 96, 96, 256 channels, 3 of them stride 2) with SiLU, not 4×4 kernels with ReLU, and the 8th conv is a zero-initialised 3×3 conv to model_channels. The ×8 downsampling gives 512 -> 64, which resolves the draft's 32×32-vs-64×64 doubt. No explicit Gaussian initialisation is visible in REPO.

Zero convolution count: 13 zero-initialised 1×1 convs (12 zero_convs, one per trainable input block, plus middle_block_out), plus 1 zero-initialised 3×3 conv at the end of input_hint_block, so 14 in all. Mapping the paper's Z(·; Θz1) to that last 3×3 hint conv is an inference: the code has no separate 1×1 zero conv on the condition.

Each ControlNet output k is added to the locked skip feature hs[k] of the same index (both lists are popped from the end); the middle output is added to the middle block's output before the decoder. This confirms the one-to-one correspondence and the add_middle -> decoder path the draft left open.

Draft says the decoder is locked. In code the decoder (output_blocks, out) is optimised when sd_locked is False and always runs with gradients; only the encoder, middle block and time MLP sit under torch.no_grad().

Draft has one time encoder. The code has two: ControlNet.time_embed (trainable) and the locked UNetModel.time_embed, both fed by timestep_embedding(t). They are recorded as time_encoder_cn and time_encoder_sd.

Text context enters both ControlNet and the U-Net, but reaches a block only through SpatialTransformer layers (TimestepEmbedSequential passes context only to SpatialTransformer). Which levels have them depends on attention_resolutions, which is not in REPO.

CFG Resolution Weighting (w_i = 64/h_i) is not implemented in REPO. The only hook is control_scales, all 1.0 by default. In log_images the unconditional CFG branch keeps the hint (uc_cat = c_cat), with a commented-out zeros alternative.
That ControlNet's blocks start as copies of SD's weights is not visible in REPO: ControlNet is built with the same architecture, but the weight copying happens in a script that is not included.
If cond['c_concat'] is None, apply_model calls the U-Net with control=None and ControlNet is not run (plain SD path).

Parent changes from the draft: cond_encoder is drawn inside controlnet (the code defines it as ControlNet.input_hint_block), and add_skip/add_middle sit inside sd_unet (they run in ControlledUnetModel.forward).
